messages.text: just... don't even know how to keep going. feels like i'm drowning and no one sees it

It sounds like you’re feeling overwhelmed and unseen, which can be incredibly painful. You’re not alone in these feelings, even though it may seem that way right now. Can you share a bit more about what’s been weighing on you lately so we can explore it together? If you’re feeling unsafe or thinking about harming yourself, please let me know so we can connect you with immediate support.
i keep thinking it would just be easier if i wasn't here... not bc i wanna die, but bc i can't stand being this useless. like everyone else is fighting their battles and i'm just... taking up space

It sounds like you’re carrying a lot of self-judgment and feeling like you don’t have a place or purpose. Those thoughts can be heavy and isolating, but they don’t mean you’re actually without value. You matter, and your presence has an impact even if it’s hard to see right now. Would you feel okay if we explored what’s making you feel “useless” and see if we can find different ways of looking at it?

yeah... my aunt and uncle raised me, gave me everything, and now i'm just some deadweight. my brother's in rehab fighting his shit and i can't even hold down a job or finish school. feels like i'm just... failing everyone

It sounds like you’re comparing your struggles to others and setting a very high bar for yourself, which can make any setback feel like failure. Your worth isn’t defined by jobs, school, or matching someone else’s journey—your experiences are valid in their own right. You’ve been through a lot, and that doesn’t mean you’re “deadweight”; it means you’re human and facing challenges. Would you like to talk about what’s been making it hard to hold down work or finish school?
everything just piles up, y'know? my body's always fighting itself, i gotta keep looking for work, and my brain won't shut up about how i'm failing... i just wanna disappear for a while

It sounds like you’re under constant pressure from your health, finances, and intrusive thoughts, which can be exhausting. Wanting to disappear can be a sign you need rest, space, and support, not that you’re a failure. If those feelings of wanting to disappear start turning into thoughts of harming yourself, it’s important to reach out right away—would you like me to share some crisis support options? We can also explore small, manageable ways to ease that mental load so you’re not carrying it all alone.
i can't even afford therapy or real help... and i don't wanna dump all this on my family. they already got enough on their plate. so i just... sit with it

It’s understandable you don’t want to burden your family, but carrying this alone can make the weight feel heavier. Free or low-cost support does exist—like crisis lines, warm lines, and online peer groups—that can give you space to talk without judgment or financial strain. Would you like me to compile a list of those resources so you have them handy? You deserve to have someone hear you without adding to your family’s stress.
is it... selfish to want help but also not wanna burden anyone? like i need someone to talk to but i don't wanna make anyone else feel worse

Wanting help is not selfish—it’s a healthy and human need. You can seek support from people or services trained to listen without being burdened, so you’re not taking away from your loved ones’ energy. Having someone to talk to can actually help you cope better and protect the connections you care about. Would you like me to share ways to reach out safely and without guilt?
you said wanting help isn't selfish... but what if i'm just too broken to fix? i don't even know where to start

Feeling “too broken” is often a reflection of how overwhelmed you are, not a statement of truth about who you are. Change and healing can happen in small steps, and we can start by focusing on one manageable thing rather than trying to fix everything at once. You don’t have to map the whole journey today—just choosing to talk now is already a beginning. Would you like to begin with identifying one small thing that could ease your burden this week?
part of me wants things to get better... but the other part just doesn't believe it's possible. like i'm stuck in this loop and no matter what i do, i'll just end up back here

That feeling of being stuck in a loop can make hope hard to hold onto, especially when you’ve been through repeated challenges. It’s important to remember that loops can be interrupted, even if it’s in tiny ways at first, and that change is often gradual. Both parts of you—the one that wants better and the one that doubts—can coexist, and we can work with them gently. Would you like to explore what a very small interruption to that loop could look like for you?
what... what would even count as a small step? like, i can't even get out of bed most days. everything feels impossible

A small step could be something as simple as sitting up in bed for a few minutes, opening a window, or sending a short message to someone you trust. It doesn’t have to be big or life-changing—it’s about proving to yourself that even a tiny action is possible. Starting with the smallest doable thing can create momentum, and that matters. Would you like help brainstorming a few gentle options you could try tomorrow?
i just... don't know if tiny steps will ever add up to anything. feels like pouring water into a bucket with a hole

It’s understandable to doubt the impact when progress feels slow or fragile. Even with a bucket that has a hole, each drop matters—you can patch the hole over time, often with support and patience. Tiny steps aren’t about fixing everything overnight, but about keeping yourself connected to life while you work on the bigger repairs. Would you like to talk about what tools or supports might help “patch the hole” for you?

last week i almost didn't call my baby sister back... she just wanted to show me a drawing she made. and i was like... what's the point? but then i did, and she was so happy. and i felt... something. not good, but not totally dead inside either

That moment with your sister sounds like it gave you a small spark, even if it wasn’t fully joyful. Connection, especially with someone you care about, can sometimes be one of those “tiny steps” that quietly matter. It shows that even in heavy moments, there are parts of you still able to respond and feel. Would you like to explore ways to keep those small sparks present more often?
maybe... talking to my sister is one thing i can do that actually means something. she doesn't care if i'm broke or jobless. she just wants me to answer when she calls

That’s a powerful realization—your sister values you for who you are, not for what you achieve. Staying connected with her could be a grounding anchor while you work through everything else. It’s a reminder that you matter to someone in ways that go beyond your self-criticism. Would you like to build on that by identifying a couple more connections or activities that feel similarly meaningful?
i'll try to answer when she calls... even if i don't feel like it. it's not much, but it's something

That’s a caring and purposeful choice, and it’s exactly the kind of small step that can quietly help. Consistency in those moments can strengthen your bond and give you brief reminders of connection. It’s okay if it feels like “not much”—those are the building blocks for more. Would you like me to suggest ways to gently support yourself before and after those calls so they feel easier?
thanks for just... listening. and not saying it'll all be ok. i don't need that. i just needed someone to get it

I hear you, and I’m glad you felt understood here. Sometimes being heard without promises or pressure is what helps most in the moment. You don’t have to have all the answers right now—we can take it one step at a time together. Would you like to keep talking or pause here for now?
i think... i can try to keep going. not bc it's easy, but bc my sister needs me to answer the phone. and maybe that's enough for now

That sounds like a meaningful and tangible reason to keep moving forward, even if it’s just one call at a time. Holding onto that connection can be a steady anchor while other pieces are still uncertain. You don’t have to do everything at once—this small commitment is already important. I’m here if you want to check in again when things feel heavy.
